artifacts.summary: Research report: verified DERIVED_TIER rule table, schema rationale, on_demand semantics, precedented doc location and content outline, exact index-entry shape, and budget-safety justification for the new standards file.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system config repo, an index-entries.json entry with load_when.on_demand:true always pairs with ALL of load_when.agents/commands/task_types empty -- there is no precedent for a narrow-but-nonempty hook plus on_demand. When authoring a purely reference/standards doc that should not auto-load for any agent (e.g. because every tracked agent is already over its context-budget cap per validate-context-budgets.sh), the correct index entry shape is the fully-empty load_when object plus on_demand:true, matching contracts/convergence.md, routing.md, validation.md, and reference/artifact-templates.md.

validate-context-budgets.sh's Dead Entry Check and its derived_tier Tier-4 classification are related but distinct: Tier 4 is a classification outcome of an all-empty load_when (a total, first-match-wins function that always classifies), while on_demand:true is a separate, explicit author-stated marker that exempts an all-empty entry from being flagged dead. Setting on_demand does not change an entry's tier -- a Tier-4 entry with on_demand:true is still Tier 4, just no longer flagged as dead. This distinction is the most likely point of confusion for a future context/index-entries.json author.
